comment: The guidance on legacy systems is technical. The best-documented evidence on why technically sound deployments fail is not about legacy interfaces: the United Kingdom's Whole System Demonstrator, a randomised trial with more than six thousand patients, found neither cost-effectiveness nor improvement in quality of life, attributed to implementation difficulty, inability to integrate into existing care practice, and the absence of a working business case.

public.text: The guidance on legacy systems is technical. The best-documented evidence on why technically sound deployments fail is not about legacy interfaces: the United Kingdom's Whole System Demonstrator, a randomised trial with more than six thousand patients, found neither cost-effectiveness nor improvement in quality of life, attributed to implementation difficulty, inability to integrate into existing care practice, and the absence of a working business case.
public.suggestedRevision: Cite the Whole System Demonstrator and comparable evaluations, and draw the lesson: technical conformance and clinical plausibility do not predict adoption, so implementation capacity should be planned and financed as a distinct standing resource rather than assumed. Add that evaluations should deliberately include the populations that stand to benefit, which that trial did not, and which remains a common design fault.
